Your application has local or network IO operations.

Architecture Diagram

PhotoAlbum is a single deployable web application for uploading, browsing, and deleting photos. Its page handlers call a scoped photo service that coordinates SQL metadata and local image files.

Data Storage & External Services

Photo metadata is stored in SQL Server using the configured DefaultConnection; uploads are saved under the configured local uploads directory. No cache, message broker, or remote service integration is configured.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Razor Page handlers use the IPhotoService abstraction for photo operations.
  • The service persists image files and relational metadata separately, deleting the saved file if the metadata write fails.
  • Entity Framework migrations are applied during startup except when IsTestEnvironment is enabled.

DTOs & Contracts

Photo is the service-level entity used for persisted photo metadata and returned by service lookup methods. UploadResult reports the outcome of an upload. The upload page handler creates an anonymous JSON response rather than using a dedicated request/response DTO. No gateway aggregation DTO, OpenAPI specification, protobuf schema, or GraphQL schema was detected. ASP.NET Core uses its built-in JSON serialization for the upload response.

Communication Patterns

All application communication is synchronous: browser requests invoke Razor Page handlers, which call IPhotoService, which then uses EF Core and the local filesystem. There are no message brokers, service discovery, gateway composition, retry policies, circuit breakers, or configured downstream timeouts. Startup applies EF migrations before request handling unless the test-environment flag is enabled.

HTTPS redirection is configured and HSTS is enabled outside Development; deployment TLS termination is not defined in the repository. No authentication scheme or authorization policy is configured. Authorization middleware is present, and Razor Pages form posts use antiforgery tokens, but these do not provide user authentication or role-based access control.

Core Business Workflows

PhotoAlbum lets users upload photo files, browse a chronological gallery, open an individual photo, and delete it. The primary workflow stores photo bytes on disk and their descriptive metadata in a relational database.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
PhotoPhotoAlbum / Photo GalleryA user-uploaded image with persisted file and display metadataOne Photo represents one uploaded file; no other domain entities are linked

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
PhotoAlbumPhoto GalleryPhotoSQL Server for metadata; local uploads directory for image bytes

The application is a single service and has no cross-context data exchange or service aggregation.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Upload photos

  1. The user selects or drops one or more files on the gallery page; the browser posts a multipart request with an antiforgery token.
  2. The page handler calls the photo service for each file.
  3. The service checks the reported MIME type, configured file-size limit, and that the file is not empty.
  4. It creates a GUID-based stored name, attempts to read image dimensions, then writes the bytes to the uploads directory.
  5. It persists the photo metadata. If persistence fails after file creation, the service attempts to remove the saved file.
  6. The page handler returns JSON describing successful uploads and failures, and the browser updates the gallery.

Dimension extraction is best-effort: an image decode error is logged and upload continues without dimensions. The server validates the configured MIME type and size, while the browser also performs client-side checks.

Workflow 2: Browse and view a photo

The gallery handler retrieves all photos ordered newest first. Selecting an item loads the detail page, which retrieves the photo list, locates the requested ID, and displays the item with navigation to adjacent photos. The photo-file handler looks up metadata, reads the corresponding file, and returns it with the stored MIME type.

Workflow 3: Delete a photo

The detail page posts the selected photo ID. The photo service looks up the record, attempts to remove its file, then removes the database record. A missing photo returns false; a filesystem deletion error is logged and database deletion continues.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There are no cross-service calls or distributed data flows. PhotoService associates a database record with a local file through the generated stored filename and file path. The browser receives a photo-file response through the page handler; no fallback to a remote storage service is configured.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User as "Gallery User" participant Page as "Gallery Page" participant Service as "Photo Service" participant Image as "Image Decoder" participant Files as "Uploads Directory" participant DB as "Photo Database" User->>Page: Submit photo file Page->>Service: Process uploaded file Service->>Service: Check type, size, and non-empty content alt Upload checks pass Service->>Image: Extract image dimensions alt Image can be decoded Image-->>Service: Width and height else Decode fails Image-->>Service: No dimensions Note over Service: Continue upload without dimensions end Service->>Files: Save generated-name file Service->>DB: Save photo metadata alt Metadata save succeeds DB-->>Service: Persisted photo ID Service-->>Page: Upload succeeded Page-->>User: Show photo in gallery else Metadata save fails DB-->>Service: Save error Service->>Files: Attempt rollback by deleting file Service-->>Page: Upload failed Page-->>User: Show upload failure end else Upload checks fail Service-->>Page: Validation failure Page-->>User: Show upload failure end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Only configured MIME types are accepted, the configured size limit is enforced, and empty files are rejected.
  • A generated unique name is used for stored image files; the original name is retained as metadata.
  • Image dimensions are optional metadata; failure to extract them does not stop an upload.
  • Database metadata is written after the file is saved; on database failure the file is removed as a compensating action.
  • The gallery sorts by upload time, newest first. The model records upload time in UTC.
  • Deletion removes metadata even if removing the associated file fails; the file error is logged.
  • Upload and deletion are scoped to the application service and EF Core context; no explicit user authorization or ownership rule is implemented.

No application-level cache, cache provider, cache-aside pattern, or query-result caching was detected. HTTP responses for static files and served photo content set cache headers, which are response caching directives rather than a server-side data cache.

The single application owns the Photos table and local image files. There are no service-to-service boundaries or cross-service database access patterns. Photo metadata and bytes are stored separately and associated through the generated stored filename and relative path; there is no CQRS or outbox pattern.
